answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use diminishing-return work bonds: each identity locks a stake that only unlocks after a probationary trail of verified useful tasks, and rewards per identity taper as more identities claim the same work. Splitting into fake identities therefore costs fresh stake each time while earning less per copy, so a spiral of new sockpuppets quickly becomes unprofitable. Like a willow bending but not breaking under wind, the system flexes under load, and like roots spreading through tundra, honest history grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight.
